commit.message:
Revoke sessions on password reset and email change; use DB role

- requireAuth now checks the user's DB record: tokens issued before
  users.sessions_valid_after are rejected, tokens for deleted users are
  rejected, and the CURRENT role is used (a demoted admin loses access
  immediately instead of keeping the role in a 7-day token)
- Password reset and email change revoke all existing sessions; the email
  change issues the current device a fresh session afterwards
- DB failure returns 503 rather than 401 so a blip doesn't sign users out
- Tolerates the migration not having run yet (falls back, never breaks
  sign-in or password reset)
- requireAuth / requireAdmin / getOptionalAuth are now async; all 18 call
  sites await them
- schema.sql: add users.sessions_valid_after

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix!: revoke JWTs and role sessions when permissions are withdrawn

- tibba-cache: add RedisCache::mget and shared credential revocation
  markers (revoke_user_credentials / revoke_role_credentials /
  is_credential_revoked), checked with a single MGET
- tibba-session: revocation now uses the shared markers and also covers
  the session's roles; add revoke_role_sessions
- tibba-jwt: JwtUser rejects access tokens issued before a user/role
  revocation; requires init_revocation_cache (fail-closed 503 otherwise)
- router-user: refresh tokens record their issue time and are refused
  after the user's credentials are revoked (legacy entries fail safe)
- tibba-model-builtin: PermissionModel::soft_delete_by_code returns the
  roles that lost the permission
- tibba-rbac: add RbacAdmin (grant / revoke / delete_permission) that
  revokes affected roles' credentials after withdrawing permissions
- app: wire the JWT revocation cache at startup; reject jwt access/refresh
  TTL longer than session TTL

BREAKING CHANGE: tibba_jwt::init_revocation_cache must be called before
JwtUser is used; soft_delete_by_code returns Vec<String>; refresh token
records changed format.

fix(auth): verify token expiry and signature before trusting claims

- Tokens now carry an exp claim (JWT_TTL, default 24h) and are rejected
  once expired; previously a token was valid forever, even after the
  user was deleted.
- The signature is compared in constant time (hmac.Equal), the header
  must declare HS256, and the Authorization header must use the Bearer
  scheme.
- The middleware stores the verified claims on the request context and
  util.GetPayload reads them from there, instead of re-decoding the
  header without checking the signature.
- Member tokens carry agency_id so later checks can scope members to
  their own agency.
- Claims use lowercase JSON names (sub, role, role_id, agency_id, exp).
  Tokens issued before this change are rejected and clients must log in
  again.

fix(auth): bind tokens to the user row, not the username

Claims carried only username/role/ver and VerifyToken resolved the row
with WHERE username=?. A freshly created account starts at token_version
1, which is exactly what an un-refreshed login token carries, so deleting
a user and recreating one with the same name and role revived every
unexpired token issued to the deleted account. Both operations are
exposed on /api/admin/users, and PRODUCTION_CONTRACT states deletion
immediately rejects previously issued tokens.

No schema change needed: users.id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
which SQLite never reuses. The claim set gains uid, the refresh UPDATE
and the verification lookup match on it, and username, role and version
are still compared.

Operational note: tokens issued before this change decode to uid 0, match
no row and are rejected, so every open console session must log in once
more. The console already handles a 401 by clearing the session and
reloading, and never decodes the token itself.

Revalidate access tokens against the account on every request

Security review finding (OWASP API2 broken authentication): access
tokens lived 8 hours and carried the role and permission claims, and
nothing checked them against the account after issue. Disabling,
locking or re-roling a user, or changing their password, revoked only
refresh tokens - the access token kept working, with its old role,
until it expired.

- AccessTokenRevalidator runs on every authenticated request
  (JwtBearerEvents.OnTokenValidated), before any [Authorize] check. It
  rejects the token if the account no longer exists, is disabled or
  locked, now has a different role than the token claims, or changed
  its password after the token was issued. One indexed lookup by id.
- Tokens now carry an iat claim for that comparison; tokens without one
  (issued before this change) are refused, costing one silent refresh.
- Access tokens last 15 minutes instead of 8 hours
  (Jwt:AccessTokenMinutes, 1-480), bounding how long a change to a
  role's permission grants takes to reach a signed-in user. ClockSkew is
  30 seconds, since the API both issues and validates the tokens.
- The JWT bearer setup moved from Program.cs to
  AddMicroLimsJwtAuthentication so tests can exercise it as deployed.

A rejected token is a 401. The frontend's apiClient already refreshes on
401: an active user silently gets a token with their current role; a
disabled or locked user's refresh is refused (RefreshAsync) and they
are signed out.

Tests: AccessTokenRevalidationTests - one per rule, plus end-to-end
through the real authentication setup in a TestServer with signed
tokens and [Authorize] role checks. With the check switched off, all
five end-to-end tests fail (200 instead of 401). New JwtTokenService and
JwtConfiguration tests cover the lifetime, range check and iat claim.

Verified in the running API against PostgreSQL: token lifetime 15 min
with iat; disabling the account turns the next request into a 401 and
refresh fails; a password change invalidates the old token while a new
login works. Full suite with PostgreSQL: 1327/1327.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016341pBxZzxBCD7Ku7Z2S5F

f07(backend): admin user management

- authenticate re-reads user (isActive/role/siteId) from the DB on every

- login rejects deactivated accounts with a distinct 403.

commit.message:
Add staff session revocation and expand audit log coverage

Staff JWTs were stateless 30-day tokens with no revocation check —
deactivating a staff member or changing their role had no effect on
tokens already issued; they stayed fully authorized under the old
permissions until expiry.

Adds a tokenVersion column on staff, bumped whenever role or active
changes and embedded in the JWT at sign time. A new withFreshStaff
middleware re-checks every staff-authenticated request against the
live staff record: rejects if the account was deleted/deactivated or
the token's version is stale, and swaps in the current DB role so a
demotion applies immediately too.

Also extends audit log coverage (previously ~14 call sites, mostly
orders/returns/staff) to product edits, variant price changes, and
product/promo deletes and creates — sensitive mutations that
previously left no trail.

Verified live: a token issued before deactivation is rejected on the
next request even though it's still cryptographically valid and
unexpired; a demoted admin's old token is rejected, and a freshly
re-issued token correctly loses admin-only access; product/promo
mutations now appear in the audit log with useful metadata. Checked
the backoffice staff page renders the updated active/role state
correctly.

feat(auth): check live user state per request and add password change

- SessionGuard takes the role and active flag from the database and rejects
  tokens issued before users.tokens_valid_after (millisecond iatMs claim).
- POST /auth/change-password requires the current password, ends all other
  sessions and issues a fresh cookie.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Changing a role's permissions sends its holders back through MM OS

Editing a role in Admin > Roles, or importing a role file that changes a
role's permission list, left every holder's live service session on the old
list until it expired (15 min to 30 days depending on the service). Both
paths now write a service-scoped revocation for each holder. Services reject
only tokens issued at or before a revocation, so holders simply re-enter with
the new permissions. Renames and description edits revoke nobody.

commit.message:
Deactivation and password reset end the session at once

Access tokens issued before the cutoff are rejected on every request,
live streams re-check the session on each heartbeat and close, and the
panel returns to sign-in when the session cannot be renewed. It also
re-reads the signed-in user every minute so role changes show up.
Access tokens now live 15 minutes.

fix(admin): guard self-lockout, revoke tokens on role change, fix auth flash

Final whole-branch review found three issues in Phase 5 Plan B's admin
role-management UI:

1. An admin could demote/clear their own role via POST
   /api/admin/users/[uid]/role with no guard, locking themselves (and
   possibly the whole business) out with no self-service recovery path.
   Now rejects with 400 when the target uid is the caller's own uid and
   the requested role isn't 'admin' (self-reaffirmation still allowed).

2. A revoked/promoted role didn't take effect until the existing ID
   token naturally expired (up to ~1 hour). The role route now calls
   revokeRefreshTokens(uid) after a successful claims change, and all
   three verify-id-token.ts helpers now verify with checkRevoked: true
   so an already-issued token is rejected immediately after revocation
   instead of silently working until expiry.

3. /admin/roles reproduced the auth-flash bug already documented against
   /staff/orders in PROJECT_STATUS.md §5 (briefly shows "Not authorized"
   to a legitimate signed-in admin before the async auth check resolves).
   Fixed with the same prescribed 3-part shape: destructure loading, gate
   the effect on it, add it to the dependency array. /staff/orders itself
   is unchanged and still tracked as a known gap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(auth): separate access and refresh tokens and use current user state

- Tokens carry a tokenType claim. API requests only accept access
  tokens, so a 7-day refresh token can no longer be used as one, and an
  access token can't be used to refresh
- authenticate and refresh load the user from the database: role and
  family come from there, and disabled or deleted users are rejected
  immediately instead of when their token expires
- Access tokens issued before this change are rejected once; the
  frontend refreshes them automatically with the stored refresh token

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01S51ocUa1Ji5SxtZMRQ8rph

feat(auth): accept Lambda-issued tokens and enforce roles per endpoint

The CPF Lambda and this API now sign with the same secret, issuer and
audience, so a token from either side authenticates here. That makes
authentication alone meaningless as an authorization signal: before this
change a customer token satisfied the bare [Authorize] on every controller and
could manage inventory.

Endpoints are now split by role. Customers, vehicles, parts, services and the
service order lifecycle require a staff role; order tracking and the budget
decision — the two customer-facing operations — accept either.

Those two endpoints were [AllowAnonymous] and are not anymore. This is a
breaking change for any caller relying on unauthenticated access, and it is
required for coherence: the gateway authorizer now rejects tokenless requests
before they reach the pod, so an endpoint the application believes is anonymous
would be unreachable in practice.

Claim names are kept short (sub, role) with inbound mapping disabled, so the
same claim set works whichever side minted the token. Issuer and audience are
now validated, with platform-wide defaults matching mechanics-lambda.

Closes #241

feat(auth): harden session & tier-access integrity for role/permission changes

Add ms_user.tokenVersion (migration 0047), bumped whenever a user's role,
organization, or cross-tier wildcard access changes, or a role's permission
set is edited. middlewares.Auth() now rejects access tokens issued before
the bump, forcing re-login so a session can't keep acting on permissions
or scope that were since revoked/changed elsewhere.

Also fix Super Admin accounts being unable to access org-scoped data/portals
without a manually-granted wildcard: effectiveWildcardTierAccess() now treats
Super Admin as implicitly having full LDK/Puskomda/Puskomnas access,
regardless of the wildcardTierAccess value stored in the DB.

Add businessId claim to admin/customer JWTs

Both token types now carry businessId alongside the existing sub/role
claims. requireRole() rejects any token missing businessId, so tokens
issued before this change (and the migration in the previous commit)
stop working automatically — no separate token-versioning scheme
needed, just one forced re-login.

feat(auth): role and permission changes take effect without re-login

Owner decision (D3/D4): assigning a role/department, editing a role's matrix,
deleting a department or an SSO mapping change no longer revokes the member's
sessions. SessionService.markClaimsStale stamps `claimsAt` on every live session
(TTL kept, revoked sessions untouched) and publishes `auth:claims-changed`.
Access tokens issued before that instant get 401 TOKEN_CLAIMS_STALE from the
auth-service strategy and the shared guard (ai-service, connector-service); the
client refreshes silently and receives the new claims. Refresh pins `iat` to
`claimsAt` when this instance's clock lags. Block, password reset/change and
logout still revoke.

Also: an empty connectorAllowList means "allow all", so validateAiSettings no
longer rejects a non-empty allowedConnectors in that case.

commit.message:
Honor token revocation on disable / password / role change

JWTs are stateless, so a disabled account previously stayed valid until
expiry. Add users.creds_changed_at (migration 014), bumped on disable,
password reset and role change. The auth middleware gains an optional
Validate hook; apisrv wires a 30s-cached check that rejects tokens for
disabled accounts or tokens issued before the last credential change.

feat(security): add security-relevant logging across auth and admin actions

The codebase had zero logging anywhere (no @Slf4j, no log statements) -
login attempts, registrations, role changes, account enable/disable,
password changes, refresh token issuance/revocation and rejected JWTs
left no trace, making incidents impossible to investigate after the
fact. None of these log statements include a password, JWT, refresh
token value, or other secret - only ids, roles and outcomes.

- AuthenticationServiceImpl: log successful registration and login
  (userId + role only).
- RefreshTokenServiceImpl: log token issuance (debug), revocation
  (debug for a single token, info for a bulk revokeAllUserTokens with
  a count - this is the "new login/logout invalidates old sessions"
  path).
- UserServiceImpl: log role changes (old -> new role), account
  enable/disable, and both self-service and admin-triggered password
  changes.
- JwtAuthenticationFilter: the catch-all around JWT parsing previously
  swallowed every exception silently; now logs at debug level (method,
  path, exception message - never the token itself) before letting
  Spring Security's entry point handle the 401.
- JwtAuthenticationEntryPoint: log a warning for every unauthenticated
  request that gets rejected (method + path only).

Verified: full Spring context still boots against the local Postgres
dev database (mvn test, contextLoads passes).

chore: isolate every JWT claim check and the login/MFA token boundary in tests

The existing expiry test broke expiry, version, csrf and not-before at once,
so it could not show which check rejected the token. Each of expiry,
not-before, issued-at, missing exp, issuer, audience, subject, jti, csrf,
version, role, purpose and the HS384/HS512 algorithms is now tested as the
single defect in an otherwise valid token, the clock leeway is checked from

commit.message:
feat(auth): harden JWT handling, add RBAC + auth audit trail, self-service profile API

Closes #1287
Closes #1288
Closes #1289
Closes #1290

#1287 - Strengthen JWT security
- Every issued access/refresh token now carries iss, aud and a unique jti.
  src/config/jwt.config.ts centralises issuer, audience, pinned algorithms,
  per-token TTLs and clock tolerance.
- JwtStrategy / JwtRefreshStrategy assert issuer + audience, pin the signing
  algorithm to prevent algorithm confusion, and reject tokens with no subject
  claim. Refresh tokens are scoped to a separate audience so one can never be
  replayed as an access token.
- TokenRevocationGuard (registered globally) rejects revoked access tokens
  before business logic, matching on either the raw token or the jti. This
  closes the window where a leaked access token stayed usable for its full
  15-minute lifetime after logout.
- Password reset request and completion now revoke every outstanding session, so
  a stolen refresh token cannot survive a credential change.

#1288 - Role-based access control
- Added the SUPPORT role alongside USER/HEALER/ADMIN, and a canonical
  ROLE_PERMISSIONS map as the single source of truth for what a role grants.
- RbacGuard (registered via APP_GUARD) enforces @Roles and @Permissions
  consistently on every route, so access control no longer depends on a handler
  remembering @UseGuards(RolesGuard).
- 403 responses now name the missing role/permission and carry a machine
  readable code; an unauthenticated request is a 401.
- Permission claims embedded in a token are intersected with what the role
  actually grants, so a token cannot self-escalate. Unknown roles resolve to an
  empty permission set (fail closed).

#1289 - Audit logging for auth events
- New append-only auth_event_logs entity plus AuthEventAuditService, covering
  login success/failure, lockout/unlock, logout, token refresh and revocation,
  password change/reset and email verification.
- Failed logins are recorded even when the account cannot be identified, so
  credential stuffing against unknown addresses stays visible.
- Metadata is scrubbed of passwords, tokens and TOTP codes before it is written.
  Audit write failures are swallowed so a valid login can never become a 500.
- Rows carry a computed retention date; purgeExpired() applies the configured
  AUTH_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS window (default 180).
- Admin-only read endpoints for listing events, per-user activity summary and
  the active retention policy.

#1290 - User profile update API
- New MeProfileController mounted at users/me/profile. It takes no identifier,
  so there is no code path to address another account.
- UpdateMeProfileDto is an allowlist (firstName, lastName, phoneNumber, avatar)
  and the pipe runs with forbidNonWhitelisted, so attempts to set role, status,
  isVerified, password, walletBalance or any other sensitive field are rejected
  with 400 instead of being silently dropped.
- MeProfileService re-checks the allowlist at runtime as defence in depth,
  recomputes fullName, returns 409 for a phone number owned by another account,
  and responds with the freshly read row so the caller sees persisted values.

commit.message:
fix(auth): bind JWTs to an issuer and audience

SEC-03. Access tokens carried sub/role/exp/iat/jti but no iss and no aud, so
anything else signed with the same key -- a future service sharing the
signing secret, a differently scoped token -- would be accepted verbatim.

- create_access_token now stamps iss="bangla-gpt-api" and
  aud="bangla-gpt-clients" (settings-configurable: jwt_issuer,
  jwt_audience).
- decode_token verifies both, and because issuer/audience are required by
  PyJWT, a token missing either is refused. Every token minted before this
  change lacks the claims and is rejected, forcing a one-time re-login; the
  impact is bounded to the 60-minute access-token lifetime and the F-05
  session-epoch design already handles rotation.

The finding also required either refresh rotation with reuse detection or a
written decision for the substitute. The substitute is the session-epoch +
short-lifetime + per-token jti-revocation design, and that decision is
recorded in ADR-0010. ADR-0008's password-hashing clause is marked superseded
(rehashing moved to Argon2id in AUD-0023).

test_jwt_claims.py: token carries the claims; wrong issuer and wrong audience
are rejected; a pre-change token (no iss/aud) is refused. test_security still
sees ExpiredSignatureError for an expired token (PyJWT validates exp before
audience/issuer). No other hand-crafted-token test needed changes
(test_password_reset's legacy token is derived from a decoded token and keeps
its claims; test_auth_teacher's forged/expired tokens are rejected regardless
and assert only 401).

Verification: 32 passed across test_jwt_claims, test_security,
test_auth_teacher and test_password_reset; ruff clean.

Refs: AUD-0028
